limitations: Object reads come from an in-memory store: S3 latency is not measured.
Embeddings are the offline hash embedder; its CPU cost (single thread, in the worker process) is real but a provider's network latency is not.
Jobs are enqueued directly through the production queue producer; the outbox dispatcher and recovery sweeps are not exercised.
Plain-text documents only; PDF parsing is not measured.

Everything runs on one machine: PostgreSQL is limited to 2 CPUs, but the worker process, Redis and Docker share the host, so absolute numbers are hardware-bound and CPU contention between them is possible.

Scenarios share one database, so tables grow between them. The concurrency comparison rotates the order of levels over whole rounds (each level in each position equally often) to cancel a linear growth effect; non-linear effects (autovacuum, checkpoints, cache warmth) remain, and the per-scenario starting row counts are reported so they can be inspected.

Concurrency 1, 2 and 4 are compared with identical documents, but only on this host: the worker's single event loop makes CPU-bound stages (parse, chunk, hash embedding) contend for one thread, so higher concurrency mainly overlaps database and child-process waits.
Client-observed SQL timings include event-loop delay; no database-server execution time is measured.
No fault was injected: failures, retries and timeouts reported are only those that happened.
The run is of the current schema only: there is no content_tsv column to compare against.

measurements.endToEndMs: Enqueue to the end of the activation call, in the benchmark process. Includes queue wait.
measurements.processingMs: Worker-side: first claim call to the end of the activation call. Excludes queue wait.
measurements.activationTxMs: Client-observed: begin to commit round trip of the activation transaction (includes event-loop delay in the worker process).
measurements.clientSqlMs: Every '*ClientMs' field is client-observed: statement sent to result received by the pg driver. It includes network, driver and event-loop scheduling delay, so it is NOT PostgreSQL execution time.
measurements.serverExecution: Not measured: pg_stat_statements is not enabled in the disposable container. No field reports database-server execution time.
measurements.eventLoop: Event-loop delay (10 ms sampling) and utilization of the worker process per scenario. Delay inflates every client-observed timing.
measurements.cpu: workerCpuCores is process CPU time over wall time (1.0 = one saturated core; the worker's event loop is single-threaded). postgresCpuCores is container CPU time over wall time against a 2-core limit.
measurements.saturation: A scenario is flagged when the worker event loop utilization or worker CPU is at least 0.9 of one core, or PostgreSQL uses at least 0.9 of its CPU limit: its client timings then include queuing, not only work.

plan: sequential, concurrency 1, 10x each of small/medium/large/max (after one discarded warm-up)
one document of exactly parseLimits.maxInputBytes (rejected by the parser: shows the real chunk ceiling)
20 maximum-size documents at concurrency 1, 2 (the default) and 4: 3 rounds, level order rotated per round, identical documents
one workspace of 50 mixed documents at concurrency 2
